commits.message:
feat(cron): universal redacted visibility + shared (editableByAnyone) scheduled messages

Every channel-targeted scheduled job is now visible to everyone: full rows
for the owner/admins/shared jobs, identity-and-schedule-only redacted rows
otherwise; DM-targeted and channelless personal jobs stay invisible to
non-owners on every read path. A new editableByAnyone flag (skills
precedent) opens edit/disable/run-now — never delete — to everyone; the
flag itself stays owner/admin. update_scheduled_message gains an enabled
field so 'turn off' can disable instead of delete, and cancel confirms its
target by name. Access control is centralized in src/tools/cronJobAccess.ts.
Home Tab Skills and Schedules regroup into Shared / Yours / Non-Accessible
sections with a shared-flag toggle, and 'editable by everyone' is renamed
'shared' everywhere.

feat(plugins): SDK reconcileCronJobs + watchFile for plugin-owned schedules

Declarative API a plugin calls during init: diff against existing
plugin === ownerKey jobs, upsert entries in specs[], delete prior
owner-jobs not in specs[]. Preserves the admin-toggled enabled flag.
Adds plugin-scoped watchFile (closed on plugin reload to avoid
cross-generation double-fires) and wires data/config.json into the
existing config watcher so plugins observe config changes for free.

CronJob gains pluginManaged/specKey for stable identity across
reconciles; update_scheduled_message / cancel_scheduled_message refuse
plugin-managed jobs. Home Tab splits the Scheduled Messages section
into user-created (full controls) and plugin (read-only +
Enable/Disable, admin-only).

build: add oxlint, oxfmt, and lefthook for linting and formatting

- Add oxlint with typescript/import/unicorn plugins and deny-warnings
- Add oxfmt formatter and establish clean baseline across all src/ files
- Configure lefthook pre-commit hook (lint, format, test in parallel)
- Add VS Code extension recommendation for oxc-vscode
- Fix all lint warnings (unused imports, useless fallbacks, etc.)
- Add tsconfig.build.json to exclude test files from production build

feat: add cron-based scheduled messages with silentThinking mode

Cron scheduler that ticks every 60s and executes matching jobs via
processMessage. Dynamic jobs spawn a Claude session; responses are
posted as top-level channel messages (silentThinking bypasses the
streaming UX).

Includes CRUD tools (create/cancel/update/list_scheduled_messages),
Home Tab management UI, resolveChannelId helper extracted from 3
tools, TriggerType extended with "scheduled", and delivery context
for non-interactive execution.

with explicit PUT-only APIs to simplify serialization, OpenAPI
generation,
and client SDKs while preserving domain event behavior.

- Remove PATCH endpoints and JsonNullable request models to eliminate
  patch-specific serialization semantics
- Add PUT-only contracts for current-user profile, preferences, and
  meeting settings to enforce full-replacement semantics and explicit
  nullable handling (null clears)
- Update OpenAPI generation to regenerate the unified spec without PATCH
  operations or JsonNullable component schemas to produce nullable-free
  API artifacts
- Update Android OpenAPI generator and networking config to disable
  nullable wrappers and remove JsonNullableModule registration to
  regenerate SDKs that do not require JsonNullable
- Remove jackson-databind-nullable dependency and
  JsonNullableJackson3Module
  from backend shared config to simplify runtime configuration
- Migrate and add tests to reflect PUT semantics, explicit password
  handling,
  timeout clearing, and LIVE auto-approval behaviors to preserve
  integrity
- Add design, proposal, specs, tasks, verification, and report artifacts
  to
  document the migration plan and validation outcomes

BREAKING CHANGE: PATCH /api/v1/me, PATCH /api/v1/me/preferences, and
PATCH /api/v1/meetings/{id}/settings are removed; clients must use the
corresponding PUT endpoints and regenerate SDKs.

Signed-off-by: Nguyễn Ngọc Phú <ngocphunguyenabc@gmail.com>

feat(api): replace patch endpoints with PUT contracts

The patch-based partial-update flows using JsonNullable added complexity
and
special-case handling. Replacing them with explicit PUT full-replace
contracts
simplifies request handling, removes the JsonNullable dependency, and
makes
password and preferences semantics explicit.

- Add PutMeetingSettingsCommand and PutMeetingSettingsUseCase to enable
  full
  replacement of meeting settings via PUT
- Add MeetingSettingsPasswordResolver to normalize raw passwords and
  compute
  hashes when replacing settings
- Add PutMeetingSettingsUseCaseTest to exercise PUT-based meeting
  settings flows
- Remove UpdateMeetingSettingsCommand, UpdateMeetingSettingsUseCase,
  UpdateMeetingSettingsRequest and related JsonNullable patch DTOs to
  drop the
  PATCH-based flow
- Update MeetingController and presentation DTOs to accept PUT-based
  settings
  requests to align the API surface with full-replace semantics
- Add PutPreferencesCommand, PutUpdatePreferencesUseCase and
  UserPreferencesSerializer to replace preference merge-patch with
  explicit
  replacement and JSON serialization
- Refactor user profile update to replaceProfile and adjust AvatarUpdate
  variants
  to reflect full-profile replacement intent
- Remove JsonNullableJackson3Module configuration and drop
  jackson.databind.nullable from several service build files to
  eliminate the
  JsonNullable transitive requirement
- Add CommonErrorCode.METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED and expand
  GlobalExceptionHandler
  imports to handle additional web error cases

BREAKING CHANGE: Several PATCH endpoints and JsonNullable-based request
DTOs were
removed and replaced by PUT full-replace endpoints (meeting settings and
user
preferences/profile). Clients must switch to the new PUT APIs and update
request
bodies/semantics accordingly.

Signed-off-by: Nguyễn Ngọc Phú <ngocphunguyenabc@gmail.com>

feat(user-management): add profile patching, queries, events

Enable partial profile updates, profile queries, and event publishing so clients
can manage profiles and downstream services can maintain local projections
without HTTP callbacks.

- Add PatchUserRequest and PatchPreferencesRequest DTOs to represent
  JsonNullable-based patch payloads
- Add PATCH /api/v1/users/me and PATCH /api/v1/users/me/preferences endpoints to
  support partial profile and per-field preference updates
- Add GetUserUseCase, GetUsersSliceUseCase and controller GET endpoints to
  expose /users/me, /users/{id}, and /users with slice pagination and filters
- Introduce UserUpdatedEvent and register it in User.updateProfile to notify
  downstream services of profile changes
- Update User aggregate and repository to handle profile updates and to support
  findActiveUsers returning paginated slices
- Update UserPreferencesParser, add UserPreferencesResponse and update
  Login/Refresh/Preferences use cases to return output DTOs to separate
  input/output contracts
- Update JacksonConfig and build.gradle to register JsonNullableJackson3Module
  and add jackson-databind-nullable dependency to enable JsonNullable support
- Add JPA query (findActiveFiltered) and adapt UserRepositoryAdapter to map
  Slice to PageResult to enable filtered slice queries
- Add unit and integration tests to validate profile patching, preference
  merging, queries, and event publishing

Signed-off-by: Nguyễn Ngọc Phú <ngocphunguyenabc@gmail.com>

refactor(shared): reorganize shared package namespace and errors

Standardize shared package layout and centralize web error handling to avoid
naming collisions and improve cross-service reuse.

- Remove legacy domain and web classes to migrate to namespaced layout
- Add namespaced ValueObject to provide a canonical shared domain interface
- Add CommonErrorCode to centralize infra-level error codes across services
- Add ErrorCode marker interface to unify service-specific error enums
- Add GlobalExceptionHandler to map validation and unexpected exceptions to
  JSend
- Update violation code resolution to normalize constraint codes to
  ViolationCode

Signed-off-by: Nguyễn Ngọc Phú <ngocphunguyenabc@gmail.com>

feat(elasticsearch): migrate logstash_pipeline to Plugin Framework entitycore envelope (#2750)

* feat(elasticsearch): migrate logstash_pipeline resource from Plugin SDK to entitycore envelope

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* style: fix go fmt in provider.go

* docs: add missing generated docs for kibana_dashboard and kibana_stream

* fix(docs): remove kibana_dashboard and kibana_stream docs to prevent check-docs CI failures

* chore(openspec): archive es-entitycore-migration-phase2-logstash via verify-openspec

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci: trigger checks

* fix(provider): remove migrated SDKv2 resources from old provider

The ingest_pipeline and logstash_pipeline resources were migrated to
Plugin Framework entitycore envelope but were still referenced in the
legacy SDKv2 provider, causing build failures. They are already
registered in the Plugin Framework provider (provider/plugin_framework.go).

* fix(models): remove omitempty from LogstashPipeline description

The description field needs to be sent as empty string to the API
when cleared by the user, so that Elasticsearch properly unsets it.
With omitempty, the empty string was omitted from the PUT payload,
causing the old description value to persist server-side. This was
 causing TestAccResourceLogstashPipelineOptionalUnset to fail.

* fix(entitycore): update schema factory signatures to accept context.Context

Updates the schema factory functions to match the new entitycore
NewElasticsearchResource/NewElasticsearchDataSource signatures that
now require func(context.Context) schema.Schema.

Fixes build failures caused by origin/main introducing the signature
change without updating all callers.

* fix(logstash): add defaults for description and username to match SDKv2 behavior

Adds stringdefault.StaticString("") to description and
stringdefault.StaticString("api_key") to username so that:
1) Removing description from config sends an empty string to the API
   (clearing the field), matching the old SDK behavior.
2) username defaults to "api_key" when not specified, preserving
   backward compatibility with the old SDKv2 DefaultFunc.

Fixes TestAccResourceLogstashPipelineOptionalUnset acceptance test.

* fix(logstash): revert incorrect defaults and omitempty removal, fix test expectation

Reverts the recent attempts to fix TestAccResourceLogstashPipelineOptionalUnset by:

- Removing Default modifiers from description and username (they were introducing drift)

- Restoring omitempty on LogstashPipeline.Description

- Updating the test to reflect actual Elasticsearch behavior: the API retains description when omitted from config

The previous fixes (commits 769c8be6 and 7d4a24c7) were based on an incorrect assumption that Elasticsearch clears the description field when an empty string is sent. CI across all ES versions shows the API preserves the existing value.

* fix(logstash): use jsontypes.NormalizedType for pipeline_metadata and add SDK->PF migration test

- Switch pipeline_metadata schema attribute from plain StringAttribute to
  jsontypes.NormalizedType for proper JSON normalization.
- Update Data.PipelineMetadata field from types.String to jsontypes.Normalized.
- Update readLogstashPipeline to use jsontypes.NewNormalizedValue when
  setting pipeline_metadata in state.
- Add TestAccResourceLogstashPipelineMigration acceptance test that creates
  a pipeline with the legacy SDKv2 provider (v0.14.5) via ExternalProviders
  and then verifies seamless migration to the Plugin Framework provider.

Addresses review comments on PR #2750.

## 2. Security envelope (`R/escape.R`)

Implements design.md Decision 4: typed escape-on-construction (no `paste0()` of Swift code from user data). Closes the HIGH-severity finding from closed PR #96. Supports design.md Non-Goals (no string-interpolation API).

- [x] 2.1 Create `R/escape.R` exposing `internal_escape_swift_string(s)` that takes a single R character vector and returns a Swift-string-literal-safe escape. Escapes per spec.md Requirement "Typed escape-on-construction prevents Swift code injection from user data": `"` → `\"`, `\` → `\\`, `\n` → `\\n`, `\r` → `\\r`, `\t` → `\\t`, control chars 0x00-0x1F and 0x7F → `\\u{<hex>}`, U+2028 / U+2029 → `\\u{2028}` / `\\u{2029}`. **Behavior**: input `'A\\B"C'` produces output `'A\\\\B\\"C'` (R-string repr; the underlying bytes match what Swift expects in source). **Verify**: `swift test --filter test-escape.R` (test in §6.1) passes.

- [x] 2.2 Create `R/escape_helpers.R` exposing `internal_swift_literal_string(s)` that wraps escaped output in surrounding `"..."` to produce a complete Swift string literal. Composition: `internal_swift_literal_string(s) == paste0('"', internal_escape_swift_string(s), '"')`. Centralizes the construction so future audit can `grep` for any string-literal emission going through this single chokepoint. Implements design.md Decision 4: typed escape-on-construction (centralized helper as the single chokepoint). **Verify**: `swift test --filter test-escape.R::test_swift_literal_wraps_in_quotes` passes.

- [x] 2.3 [P] Audit guard: add a CI script `tools/check-no-direct-paste.sh` that `grep`s `R/*.R` for `paste0(.*"WordEdit\\|paste0(.*"OOXMLEdit\\|paste0(.*"LensDocument\\|paste0(.*"DocxReader\\|paste0(.*"DocxWriter` patterns. Any match fails CI. Covers spec.md Requirement scenario "Injection attempt is neutralized" by preventing the construction-side bug from being introduced. **Verify**: `bash tools/check-no-direct-paste.sh` exits 0 on the Phase 1 codebase.

## 3. Document state + anchor types (`R/document.R`, `R/anchor.R`)

- [x] 3.1 Create `R/document.R` exposing `wb_document(baseline = NULL, output = NULL)` that returns an opaque list-typed state object with fields: `baseline` (NULL or character path), `output` (NULL or character path; resolved at `wb_export` time if NULL), `steps` (initially `list()`), `generator_meta` (the generator-name + version string for the header annotation). Mirrors `docx-workflow-cli`'s `Anchor` enum cases. **Behavior**: `wb_anchor(after_text = "Intro")` returns `list(after_text = "Intro")` with class `wb_anchor`. **Verify**: `swift test --filter test-anchor.R` passes; passing two non-NULL args raises an error.

- [x] 4.2 [P] Create `R/structure.R` exposing `wb_remove_paragraph(state, anchor)` and `wb_link(state, text, url, anchor)`. Both runtime-functional Phase 1 step types per design.md Decision 3. Append step records with appropriate `type` field values (`"remove_paragraph"`, `"wrap_link"`). Covers spec.md Requirement "Phase 1 step-type coverage matches docx-workflow-cli's shipped + pending split". **Verify**: `swift test --filter test-structure.R` passes for the two functions.

- [x] 4.3 [P] Create `R/inline.R` exposing `wb_run_bold(state, text, anchor)`, `wb_run_italic(state, text, anchor)`, `wb_run_underline(state, text, anchor)`. `wb_run_bold` is runtime-functional (`OOXMLEdit.setBold`); the other two are Phase 2c-pending (will emit `try?`-wrapped Swift per design.md Decision 3). Each appends a step record marked Phase 2c-pending; emit-side (§5) wraps the corresponding Swift in `try?`. Monorepo restructure, image enrichment platform, Next.js + React 19, prod hardening

This squashes the dev line (67 commits) into the master publish. It is a large
jump spanning a full frontend rewrite, a new enrichment plane, a workspace
monorepo, major dependency upgrades, and production hardening.

Frontend: migrate to Next.js
- Replace the old Create-React-App frontend (react-photoswipe, Redux) with a
  Next.js app: album/list/single views, login/logout, 404, index redirect.
- Global state is SWR hooks + local React state (Redux fully removed).
- Base-path support via PUBLIC_URL / NEXT_PUBLIC_* (basePath + assetPrefix),
  build-time sentinels rewritten at container start so one image serves any path.
- Disable Next telemetry; fix build directory, navbar-on-load, refresh handling.

Image enrichment platform (optional, isolated plane)
- OCR (native Tesseract), semantic/"smart" search (local CLIP via onnxruntime,
  no cloud), embedded IPTC/XMP caption indexing, and geo enrichment (EXIF +
  offline GeoNames reverse-geocode) with a Leaflet map UI (supercluster).
- Reached only through the gallery's authenticated /api/v1/enrich/* proxy; the
  service is not host-exposed in prod and the gallery works with it fully down.
- Hash-keyed idempotent pipeline with per-enricher versioning + failure
  visibility; pluggable enrichers; non-blocking triggers + status.
- Real stat-gated delta scan (daily cron) vs on-demand full scan; reap of
  orphaned/stale index docs (manual admin action); accurate per-scan progress
  counts; fix idle-vs-unknown status reporting.
- Tier-1 OCR quality knobs + profiling bench; cap OCR input resolution
  (OCR_DOWNSCALE); only the canonical path refreshes a doc's stat.
- Split the BullMQ worker into its own process so heavy CLIP/OCR inference never
  blocks the API /health or search.

Monorepo + runtime config
- Move to an npm-workspaces monorepo (gallery/, enrichment/, packages/*) with
  scoped per-service Docker images built from the repo root.
- Shared rpg-config package; CONFIG_PATH for runtime config with one-time
  AUTH_PATH legacy migration; admin-managed exclude-dirs (albums/cache/walk).

Admin / user management
- User CRUD (create/delete/reset) with scrypt-hashed passwords.
- Read-only enrichment config panel (worker vs service), one-shot coverage panel,
  and OCR stats panel.

Dependency upgrades
- React 18 -> 19, react-leaflet 4 -> 5, Express 5, chokidar 5, eslint 10,
  meilisearch client 0.41 -> 0.58, and assorted minors.
- Pin Meili (v1.47.0) and Redis (8.x) images to explicit versions matching prod;
  fix the Meili volume mount path.

Security
- Override postcss to patched 8.5.x (GHSA-qx2v-qp2m-jg93).
- Derive auth-bypass test coverage from the live Express router so a new
  unauthenticated route fails CI.

UX / bugfixes
- Search: infinite scroll (remove the 100-result cap), date sort chooser,
  favorite star + lightbox deep-linking, restore results/lightbox on Back.

feat(installer): prompt for legal page configuration (#416)

* feat(installer): prompt for legal page configuration (#414)

Add an interactive "Legal pages" section to install.sh, positioned
after the infrastructure block and before password generation. Applies
to all deployment modes (data-node writes to api.legal_content via the
importer; ui/data-node-ui generates HTML files via docker-entrypoint).

Three options:
  1. Generate from contact details — prompts for IMPRESSUM_NAME,
     IMPRESSUM_ADDRESS, IMPRESSUM_EMAIL (required) and IMPRESSUM_ORG,
     IMPRESSUM_PHONE, SITE_URL (optional)
  2. Link to existing pages — prompts for IMPRESSUM_URL, PRIVACY_URL,
     SITE_URL
  3. Skip — adds empty vars to .env with comment for manual editing

The generated .env block writes SITE_URL plus either the override URLs
or the full set of IMPRESSUM_* contact vars depending on which path
the operator chose.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(installer): split comma-separated COMPOSE_PROFILES into separate --profile flags

Docker Compose v2 does not accept comma-separated values for --profile.
When AUTO_UPDATE=true the profile string became "data-node-ui,auto-update"
which was treated as a single unknown profile name, producing "no service
selected" and preventing the stack from starting.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(app): always generate and link legal pages regardless of IMPRESSUM_* config

Legal button was hidden whenever impressumUrl/privacyUrl were null, which
happened when neither IMPRESSUM_URL nor SITE_URL was set. Both pages must
always be reachable so operators without a public domain still comply with
TMG §5.

- Fall back impressumUrl/privacyUrl to relative /impressum and /datenschutz
  when no external URL or SITE_URL is configured
- Always generate impressum.html (placeholder when IMPRESSUM_NAME/ADDRESS absent)
- Always generate datenschutz.html (placeholder when template data absent)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(hub): always show legal icons per backend in instance drawer

Icons were conditional on impressumUrl/hasLegal, hiding them for backends
without SITE_URL configured. Legal links must always be visible regardless
of backend config. If no URL and no has_legal, clicking shows
"Keine rechtlichen Angaben verfügbar" instead of a failing RPC attempt.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(app): remove conditional guard from standalone legal button

The Scale button was guarded by {#if impressumUrl || privacyUrl}. Since
the entrypoint now always provides at least /impressum and /datenschutz,
the guard is never needed in production. Removing it makes the component
consistent with the always-visible design intent.

Update Playwright tests to reflect that legal buttons are always present
in both standalone and hub mode. Hub tests now assert the "Keine
rechtlichen Angaben verfügbar" modal when no URL and no has_legal.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(review): apply code review patches from PR #416 review

- Quote IMPRESSUM_* values in .env output to prevent # comment truncation
- Add info prop to LegalContentModal for neutral (non-error) messages
- Hub drawer: show backend name in "no legal data" message, use neutral
  info path instead of red error styling for unconfigured backends
- LegalModal: show neutral fallback when both impressumUrl and privacyUrl
  are null (covers local dev / misconfigured deployments)
- Update spec: always-visible button/icons, hasLegal as get_legal trigger

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(tests): update control-btn count in hub smoke test

Scale (legal) button is now always rendered unconditionally, adding a
third .control-btn to the top-right controls cluster.

Validator now enforces the grapheme-first rules exactly: oversized
leaves legal only as single whole Characters, undersized leaves only
under the per-adjacent-leaf starvation predicate, seams never inside a
cluster; new 2,000-op seed validates after every operation. The exact
predicate immediately caught a real producer gap — insert-overflow and
construction splits starved in isolation without consulting neighbors
([2048, 2045] + 4-byte insert at 3071 left an illegal 1023 leaf).
Producer now shares the validator's predicate (isBoundaryStarved) and
redistributes starved chunks with adjacent leaves. Suite: 569 + 80
green including four 10,000-op sampled seeds.

fix(rope): grapheme-first split points with balanced redistribution (DEF-001, DEF-007)

Replaces balancedSplitPoint's window-ignoring fallback and the
backward-only splitPoint walk with a bidirectional Character-boundary
search: shared leadingChunkEnd for construction and leaf splits,
rebalancedChunks yielding 1-3 balanced chunks for merge/seam
combinations, minimal-shortfall splits under boundary starvation, and
whole-cluster oversized leaves per ADR-012. repairCRLFSeam returns
overflow siblings; merge no longer retries a failed split. 13 new
red-first regression tests; one tie-direction expectation updated per
design D1 (justified inline). Suite: 559 + 80 green.

fix(rope): leaf split point moves from greedy max to midpoint with boundary adjustment

leafSplitPoint now targets the UTF-8 midpoint (capped at maxChunkUTF8) and
snaps backward to the nearest extended-grapheme-cluster boundary, so both
halves stay at or above minChunkUTF8 whenever the chunk is at least twice
the minimum, no half ever exceeds the maximum, and neither CRLF pairs nor
grapheme clusters are split (the old code cut at raw byte offsets, which
scalar-aligned on slicing but could still split clusters, and overflowed
max by one byte to hop a straddling CRLF). Construction's chunkEnd
delegates to the same boundary-snapping splitPoint. The degenerate case of
a single cluster longer than the target keeps the raw-offset cut.

Closes m2-rope-insert 1.1 and audit c3. An insert-only 4-seed probe shows
the insert path fully clean of undersized and oversized leaves, so the
stress run's non-strict max-overflow matcher is removed and the undersized-
leaf matcher is re-scoped to the delete path alone, cited to m2-rope-delete
1.3; the inner-node matcher stays cited to m2-rope-delete 3.4.

fix(rope): root-leaf insert re-chunks instead of promoting an oversized sibling

A large insert into a single-leaf rope used to split once and promote the
arbitrarily oversized remainder as the root's sibling (audit c1). The
root-leaf path now splices into the chunk and, on overflow, rebuilds via
the construction chunk distribution, so every produced leaf lands within
minChunkUTF8...maxChunkUTF8 at any insert size.

Flips the strict marker in testInsertCausingLeafSplit ahead of the S5
midpoint-split slice — that fixture inserts into a single-leaf rope, so
the re-chunked root-leaf path already satisfies the min-chunk invariant;
marker removed. Interior-leaf splits keep the greedy split point until
m2-rope-insert 1.1 lands.

fix(rope): construction never emits undersized tail chunks or groups

Chunking now balances the last two chunks when the remainder would fall
below minChunkUTF8, and steps back before a straddling CR instead of
overflowing maxChunkUTF8 past the LF. Tree grouping likewise balances the
last two groups when the tail would fall below minChildren (fires at
9-11 and 17-leaf sizes).

Flips the strict debt markers in testCRLFNotSplit (both halves: the
undersized tail and the CRLF max+1 overflow, since construction now cuts
before the pair) and testLargeString; markers removed. The delete-path
fixtures that relied on construction's old greedy leaf layout are re-aimed
at layouts that still exhibit the m2-rope-delete 1.3 debt (undersized leaf
whose neighbor cannot absorb it without overflowing max); the construction-
seeded CRLF overflow marker in testDeleteLeafMergeDoesNotSplitCRLF is
removed because that debt class no longer exists. Closes m2-rope-foundation
5.3 and 5.5.

refactor(rope): extract split logic into the spec-named Node+Split seam

leafSplitPoint existed in three drifting copies (Construction, Insert,
Delete) — the divergence REVIEW.md #1 flagged. Node+Split.swift now
holds the single canonical Substring implementation plus splitLeaf()
and splitInner() as Node methods, per m2-rope-insert 1.2 and 2.2.
Pure refactor: the split-point algorithm is unchanged (still greedy
maxChunkUTF8); the midpoint split lands with m2-rope-insert 1.1, and
the stress test's known-issue citation now points there.

Closes m2-rope-insert task 1.2 (2.2 was already done).

anchor_commit_observation.message:
Wireframe layout preview: oblique projection toggle (#197)

* task(sm-afiu): add ObliqueProjection cabinet projection primitive

Pure cabinet-projection module in packages/geometry per design.md D1:
projectPoint maps Point3D to Point2D with y-up math, depth foreshortened
by CABINET_PROJECTION (angle pi/6, depthScale 0.5).

* task(sm-5vz0): add wireframe scene builder bin face polygons

buildWireframeScene in apps/web/src/ui/wireframeScene.ts produces top,
front, and right face WireframePolygons per resolvable placed bin at
its projected box corners, per design.md D2: constraint color as a
literal fillColor on the top face, token names (resolved at paint
time) on front/right and the unconstrained fallback.
Unresolved binIds are skipped.

* task(sm-eo05): add space outline, painter ordering, and scene bounding box

Extends wireframeScene.ts per design.md D3/D5: space box edges (floor,
top, four verticals) when w/l/h are defined, floor-only degradation
when h is undefined; bin polygons sorted back-to-front by descending
origin[2], then ascending origin[0] (the viewer sits on the +x side,
so the larger-x neighbor must paint over its left neighbor), then
binId as a final determinism tie-break. buildWireframeScene now
returns { polygons, boundingBox } so the painter can translate-to-fit
without scaling.

* task(sm-a7op): add wireframe toggle and canvas painter in LayoutCanvas

Wires buildWireframeScene into the layout view per design.md D4/D5:
a local useState toggle (data-testid=wireframe-toggle, aria-pressed)
rendered alongside the canvas; the paint effect branches to the
existing drawSpaceBounds/drawPackedLayout path when off, or the new
paintWireframe painter when on, translating the scene by its bounding
box to fit the canvas without scaling. Colors resolve from CSS tokens
at paint time so theme repaint keeps working; adds the
--color-canvas-wireframe-surface token for non-top bin faces.
Toggle state is local UI state, excluded from the store and
serialization. Verified in-browser with Playwright: toggling flips
aria-pressed, the canvas and validity badge stay visible/unchanged,
and the wireframe renders as an oblique box scene.

* task(sm-v5cd): add e2e coverage for wireframe preview toggle flow

Playwright spec asserts the toggle's aria-pressed flips true/false and
that the canvas and layout-validity-badge remain visible and unchanged
in both modes. No pixel assertions -- geometry correctness lives in

feat(api): reconcile-time confirmed-total override + 409 payload (KAN-188 1/3) (#211)

* docs(openspec): KAN-188 reconcile-time-surfaces proposal, spec, tasks

* feat(api): add confirmedTotalHours override to ReconcileTimeBody

Adds a mutually-exclusive confirmed-total override field alongside the
existing additive addHours field on ReconcileTimeBody. A request
providing both is rejected with a 400 at schema validation, before any
reconcile side effect runs (KAN-188).

* feat(api): support confirmed-total override in reconcileIssueTime

Extends ReconcileOpts with confirmedTotalHours. When present, the
reconcile writes a single corrective TimeEntry (positive or negative
delta against the current total) tagged via: "reconcile-override",
instead of the additive reconcile-manual top-up. Negative corrections
set adjustsId per the ppm-engine invariant #3 DB CHECK. The additive
addHours branch is skipped whenever the override is present, as
defense-in-depth behind the schema-level mutual-exclusion 400
(KAN-188). Preserves the existing +1ms timeConfirmedAt stamp and >=
staleness comparison unchanged.

* test(api): characterize 409 payload hours for reconcile client surfaces

Adds tests proving (pre-existing behavior, no code change) that the
RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED 409 AppError.details carries a concrete
totalHours for the single-issue transitionIssue path and a per-issue
blockedIssues[].totalHours for the batch/group path. This documents the
contract the MCP and web client 409-plumbing work (PR2/PR3) depends on
(KAN-188).

* docs(openspec): mark KAN-188 Phase 1 tasks and 2.1 complete for PR1 (api)

* fix(api): status-aware anchor + no-anchor guard for reconcile override

The negative corrective TimeEntry's adjustsId anchor was picked as the
entry with max createdAt, ignoring status. This could link the entry
to a draft/submitted/rejected or cross-member entry, corrupting the
adjustment audit trail. Restrict anchor selection to approved entries
only, and throw RECONCILE_NO_ANCHOR (409) when a downward correction
has no approved anchor, instead of writing a negative entry with
adjustsId: null (defense-in-depth for the DB CHECK constraint).

* fix(api): cap confirmedTotalHours to 2 decimal places

TimeEntry.hours is Decimal(8,2); the override regex allowed more than
2 decimal places (e.g. "4.999"), which Postgres would silently
truncate, diverging the stored total from the confirmed value.
Tighten confirmedTotalHours's regex to at most 2 decimals; addHours
is unchanged.

* test(api): integration coverage for reconcile-time downward override

Exercises the confirmedTotalHours override against the real Postgres
test DB: a downward correction with an approved anchor succeeds with
no CHECK-constraint violation, the confirmed total matches exactly,
and timeConfirmedAt clears the review→done gate. Also covers the
RECONCILE_NO_ANCHOR 409 guard end-to-end when no approved entry
exists to anchor the correction to.

* docs(kan-188): record review-fix pass on tasks.md

Documents the 3 confirmed review fixes applied on top of the already-
completed Phase 1 tasks: status-aware adjustsId anchor + no-anchor
guard, confirmedTotalHours decimal cap, and new integration coverage
against the real test DB.

* test(api): fix schedule-timeline forecast-window time-bomb assertions (STL-11/STL-20)

Pre-existing CI breakage independent of KAN-188 reconcile work: two
assertions became stale when the wall clock entered July 2026.

An overdue OPEN (todo) issue with a past plan is lazily forecast on read
(KAN-161) and anchored to today (KAN-145), so it overlaps a window
containing today via its forecast span. The tests assumed this could not
happen; they passed only while CI's clock was before the window.

- STL-11: assert both the plan-overlap and the today-anchored
  forecast-overlap rows are returned (2 rows), and lock the overdue open
  todo's forecastStart/forecastEnd to start-of-day today (computed
  dynamically, not hardcoded). Bare issue stays excluded.
- STL-20: make the hidden issue terminal (done + past completedAt) so it
  is exempt from today-anchoring and stays genuinely out of window,
  preserving the envelope hidden-count contract (projectTotal 4,
  unscheduled 2).

feat(web): reconcile modal + transition intercepts + e2e gate (KAN-188 3/3) (#213)

* fix(web): preserve error details on ApiError

ApiError dropped the parsed response body's `details` field, so 409
RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED payloads carrying captured hours never reached
callers. Extend ApiError with an optional `details` property populated
from the error response body, mirroring the mcp KanonApiError fix.

* feat(web): add ReconcileModal component

Confirm-or-adjust modal shown before a transition to done completes
when the issue has unconfirmed captured time. Mirrors close-cycle-dialog's
FocusTrap/useEscapeKey/useBackdropClose pattern. Requires explicit
confirmation -- no one-click silent path. Validates the adjusted total
client-side (non-negative, <=2 decimals, <=744) matching the server rule.

* feat(web): reconcile-on-409 intercept in useTransitionMutation

Single-issue transition to done now surfaces a reconcileState instead
of the generic revert toast when blocked by 409 RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED.
Adds confirmReconcile(hours) which POSTs reconcile-time then retries the
transition, and cancelReconcile() to dismiss. The existing onSettled
cache invalidation (issueKeys/cycleKeys) is unchanged and still fires
after a reconcile-then-transition succeeds.

Also fixes the pre-existing test's wholesale @/lib/api-client mock,
which stripped ApiError and broke the new instanceof check.

* feat(web): per-issue reconcile intercept in useGroupTransitionMutation

Group/batch transition to done now surfaces blockedIssues (each with
its own captured hours) instead of the generic revert toast when the
409 payload carries blockedIssues: [{key, totalHours}]. Non-blocked
issues in the same batch already transitioned successfully.
confirmReconcile(issueKey, hours) reconciles and re-transitions that
single issue, removing it from blockedIssues on success; cancelReconcile(issueKey)
dismisses just that issue's prompt. Existing onSettled invalidation unchanged.

Also fixes the pre-existing test's wholesale @/lib/api-client mock,
which stripped ApiError and would have broken the new instanceof check.

* feat(web): wire ReconcileModal into KanbanBoard and GroupedBoard

KanbanBoard renders ReconcileModal when useTransitionMutation surfaces
reconcileState (single-issue drag to done). GroupedBoard renders one
ReconcileModal at a time for each entry in useGroupTransitionMutation's
blockedIssues, so every blocked issue gets its own confirm step with its
own hours; a non-blocked issue in the same batch never shows a modal.

* docs(openspec): mark KAN-188 Phase 4 tasks complete for PR3 (web)

* fix(web): catch reconcile+retry rejection in both transition hooks

confirmReconcile ran the reconcile-time POST and retried transition with
no try/catch, and both boards called it as `void confirmReconcile(...)`.
A rejection (e.g. 409 RECONCILE_NO_ANCHOR on a downward correction with no
approved anchor, or a failed retry) became an unhandled promise rejection:
no toast, stuck modal, zero user feedback.

Wrap both hooks' reconcile-then-retry in try/catch and surface failures
via the existing toast mechanism. useTransitionMutation now only clears
reconcileState once the full sequence succeeds, so a retry failure after
a successful reconcile leaves the modal actionable instead of stranding
the user. useGroupTransitionMutation keeps the issue in blockedIssues on
failure so it can be retried, covering the per-issue transitionIssue()
call that runs outside useMutation and was previously fully unhandled.

* fix(web): wire isSubmitting into ReconcileModal to prevent double-submit

ReconcileModal already guarded handleConfirm on isSubmitting, but neither
board passed the prop, so it was always false — a rapid double-click
fired confirmReconcile twice, racing two overlapping reconcile+transition
sequences for the same issue.

Expose isSubmitting from both useTransitionMutation and
useGroupTransitionMutation (true while reconcile+retry is in flight) and
pass it through at both KanbanBoard and GroupedBoard call sites.

* refactor(web): extract shared reconcile-api module from both transition hooks

toFiniteHours, the reconcileTime POST helper, and the
"RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED" error-code string were duplicated byte-for-byte
across useTransitionMutation and useGroupTransitionMutation — a hand-typed
API contract with real drift risk.

Move them into features/board/reconcile-api.ts (with a
RECONCILIATION_ERROR_CODE constant) and import from both hooks. Each
hook keeps its own state (reconcileState vs. blockedIssues) since that
part is legitimately different. Also collapsed the double-cast in
parseBlockedIssues to a single `entry as Record<string, unknown>`.

No behavior change — full existing reconcile test suite stays green
through the refactor, plus new unit coverage for the extracted module.

* test(web): pin GroupedBoard multi-issue reconcile sequencing (KAN-188)

Adds a stateful-mock integration test proving blockedIssues[0]-driven
sequencing surfaces each blocked issue's OWN reported hours in turn:
confirm TEST-1 (5h) -> modal re-seeds with TEST-2's own 2.5h, not a
stale value -> cancelling TEST-2 leaves it un-transitioned and closes
the modal.

No production code change — this locks down behavior that was already
correct but untested at the sequencing level.

* fix(web): correct misleading transition body comment; use role queries

use-transition-mutation.ts's docblock claimed the wire body is
{ toState }, but the actual payload (confirmed correct) is { to_state }.
Fixed the comment only — no behavior change.

reconcile-modal.test.tsx: switched button interactions from
data-testid queries to getByRole("button", { name }) where the visible
label already supports it, closer to how a user finds these controls.

* docs(kan-188): record PR3 review-fix pass on tasks.md

Documents the 5 confirmed review fixes applied to PR3 (web) after
Phase 4 completion: reconcile+retry error handling, isSubmitting
wiring, the shared reconcile-api extraction, the multi-issue
sequencing regression test, and the minor comment/query cleanups.

* test(e2e): add cross-surface regression gate for reconcile-time-to-done (KAN-188)

Adds the load-bearing e2e proving start_work -> stop_work -> transition->done
succeeds through a real web UI drag-and-drop and real api calls, asserting the
409 RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED payload surfaces as a visible ReconcileModal (not
silently swallowed) before the retried transition reaches done. Also adds an
apiDelete e2e helper (no Content-Type header on a bodyless DELETE, matching
Fastify's rejection of empty JSON bodies).

* docs(kan-188): mark Phase 6 e2e regression gate complete

* fix(web): guard blockedIssues[0] access for noUncheckedIndexedAccess (KAN-188)

* test(api): make forecast milestone-rollup tests date-robust (pre-existing time-bomb)

The '7.5 — milestone rollup' upcoming/at_risk tests seeded fixed calendar
targets. Milestone rollup derives status from forecastEnd vs (target -
atRiskBufferDays), and the engine anchors overdue work to now (KAN-145), so
forecastEnd tracks today. As real time advanced into the fixed target's buffer
window, 'resets at_risk -> upcoming' flipped to at_risk and failed at the
07-06->07-07 rollover. Seed targets relative to today so both scenarios hold on
any run date. No production code changed; assertions unchanged.

keyword definitions.

RenderNode discriminated union (Core):
- TextSpan — leaf string fragment
- CompositeNode(Summary, Body) — keyword invocation; summary from locale or
  template, body always the full recursive structural expansion
- SequenceNode — ordered list (block steps, static-effect parts)
- RulesRef(Key, DisplayText) — D18 cross-reference leaf for host link UI

TextRenderer (Archetype.Text):
- Render(KeywordNode, locale?, bindings?) — definition-time and invocation-time
  modes; ParameterRef renders as label or bound value respectively
- RenderBlock(EffectBlockDef) — SequenceNode of step renders; single-step
  returns node directly
- RenderStaticEffect(StaticEffectDef) — contribution + trigger + lifetime
- RenderLifetimeSpec(LifetimeSpec) — engine.lifetime.* locale keys with OR join
- Resolve(keyword, locale?, bindings?) — D18 lazy rules-reference expansion
- FlattenToText(RenderNode) — public static helper

Template resolution order: locale > TextTemplate > structural fallback.
Definition-time body renders cached per (KeywordDefinition, locale) via
ConditionalWeakTable; invocation-time renders not cached (vary per call).
D18 tag parsing: [display](key) and [key] produce RulesRef leaf nodes.

All 34 built-in keywords now carry a default TextTemplate for structural
text rendering without requiring a locale file.

Implementation decomposition for the skill-evals strategy. Phased so the cheap, deterministic, high-ROI layers (L1, L2) land and gate first; LLM-in-loop layers (L3, L4) follow. Each phase is independently shippable.

## 1. L1 — Script unit tests (gate the tests that already exist)

- [ ] Add `scripts/run-skill-tests.sh`: discover every `plugins/*/skills/*/scripts/test.sh` (`find ... | while read`, never `for N in $(...)`), run each, fail on any non-zero exit, summarize pass/fail per skill.
- [ ] Add `.github/workflows/skills-ci.yml` with an L1 job that runs `scripts/run-skill-tests.sh` on PRs touching `plugins/**`. Mark it a required check.
- [ ] Backfill `test.sh` for script-backed skills that lack one (audit `plugins/*/skills/*/scripts/` for scripts without a sibling `test.sh`).
- [ ] Update `plugins/_shared/script-authoring.md`: `test.sh` is mandatory for any script-backed skill; reference the runner + CI gate.
- [ ] Update `CLAUDE.md` (Skill Authoring Conventions) to point at the L1 gate.

## 2. L2 — Skill-doc lint (freeze the audit findings)

- [ ] Add `scripts/lint-skills.sh` (or `.ts`) with one discrete, file:line-reporting rule per check:
  - [ ] Frontmatter present (`name`, `description`) on every SKILL.md.
  - [ ] `## Input` table present where a skill documents arguments.
  - [ ] Every `<!-- include: <path> -->` directive resolves.
  - [ ] Every `plugins/_shared/*.md` citation path resolves.
  - [ ] Every relative markdown link in `plugins/**` and root `README.md` resolves.
  - [ ] README flag-matrix rows agree with the corresponding SKILL.md `## Input` table.
  - [ ] No `develop` branch reference outside designated migration docs (seed allowlist: `flowkit/MIGRATION-v4.md`, openspec archive). **Include `.github/workflows/**`** — `deploy-site.yml` cur

## 2. Bridge: pure-pi fallback handling

- [ ] 2.1 In `packages/extension/src/bridge.ts` (or a new `packages/extension/src/rjsf-fallback.ts` helper), add `runRjsfFallback(ctx, module): Promise<unknown>` implementing the three strategies (`"ctx-ui"`, `"defaults"`, `"reject"`).

## 5. Client: submit + reply lifecycle

- [ ] 5.1 In `RjsfFormView`, implement the submit handler: on AJV-validated submit, dispatch `ui_management { sessionId, action: "submit", event: view.dataEvent ?? `${module.id}:submit`, params: formData }` via the existing `usePluginSend` / `useWebSocketSend` hook. - [ ] 5.4 Wire `view.initialDataEvent` (when present): on mount, dispatch `ui_management { action: "list", event: view.initialDataEvent }`; pre-fill the form's `formData` with the first item from `session.uiDataMap[view.initialDataEvent]` once it arrives.
- [ ] 5.5 Add tests in `RjsfFormView.test.tsx`: invalid submit blocks dispatch; valid submit dispatches; `_reply({ ok: false })` surfaces banner; `_reply({ ok: true })` closes; timeout fires after 30s.

docs(openspec): add design, specs, tasks for add-extension-ui-rjsf-form

Phase 4 of the Generalized Extension UI System — design + specs delta +
tasks for the rjsf-form view kind that renders user-supplied JSONSchema7
through react-jsonschema-form with a Tailwind-themed widget set.

- design.md: 6 key decisions (RJSF lib, lazy bundle, Tailwind theme,
  submit semantics via existing ui_management channel, pure-pi fallback
  contract, schema field shape), risks/trade-offs, migration plan.
- specs/extension-ui-system/spec.md: 5 ADDED Requirements with 14
  WHEN/THEN scenarios covering rjsf-form view type, lazy load, AJV
  validation gating, async _reply lifecycle, pure-pi fallback
  enforcement, no-dangerouslySetInnerHTML invariant.
- tasks.md: 8 task groups, ~36 trackable tasks.

feat(cli): add CLI for uploading workflow bundles

Ship @workflow-engine/cli (binary: wfe) as a publishable npm package
that builds workflows from <cwd>/src/*.ts and uploads the resulting
bundle.tar.gz artifacts to a running runtime. The CLI exports a
programmatic upload() consumed directly by scripts/dev.ts — one code
path for monorepo dev and external users.

- packages/cli: citty entry, shipped default vite config, GITHUB_TOKEN
  auth (no retry, best-effort per bundle, structured error output)
- vite-plugin: auto-discover <root>/src/*.ts, drop workflows: string[]
  option, fail loudly on empty src/
- runtime: 422 body now includes specific error + optional Zod issues[]
  so the CLI can surface actionable validation errors
- workflows/: migrate cronitor.ts to src/, delete vite.config.ts
- scripts/dev.ts: TCP-poll runtime port, import { upload } from the CLI
- sdk + vite-plugin + cli: drop private: true, bump to 0.1.0,
  publishable scaffolding
